v1_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1220-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-06). With tariff changes ruled out (E-02) and ticket response times already within SLA (E-05), and 59% of disputed bills built on an ACTUAL meter read rather than an estimated one (E-01), the best-supported mechanism is a change to billing import validation rules around August that mis-processes bills based on actual reads, producing incorrect bills that drive the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).
v2_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-06). The best-supported mechanism now confirmed by evidence is that billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), compares a raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling, and because firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out June 2026) report raw readings in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13), BV-17 falsely flags valid high-consumption reads and the import rejects them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-11) and contributing to the surge. Per ER-1's revision of E-01, this confirmed mechanism does not reach the remaining 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of the 3025 total); their driver is not yet established and is tracked as an open unknown rather than asserted here.
